preregistration.expected_outcome:
Does not outperform. On the development seeds under the guard the composite's flag F1
was lower on point (-0.17) and clustered (-0.14), higher on masking (+0.28) and flat on
irrelevant_columns (-0.02, not significant). It still flagged 1.5-3.1x the review budget
on most scenarios and breached the false-positive budget on point, clustered,
contextual, categorical_rare, text_timestamp, varying_density, all_categorical and
swamping where intersection@1 met it; it also lost average precision on point and
clustered and flag stability on all_categorical. Round 4's conclusion should hold: a
composite policy belongs with a numeric review budget, not "auto".
preregistration.hypothesis:
Repeats composite-agreement-auto-v1 (round 4) on the current code. Since round 4: a
detector whose own boundary flagged more than half its fit rows no longer votes at
"auto" (UninformativeBoundaryWarning; Isolation Forest's did on half the synthetic
scenarios, which moves the composite's median-of-rates cut), 3-value columns are kept
with a fixed categorical distance, KMeans fits are reproducible, and the budgets are v4.
Does composite-agreement@1 at scoring.contamination = "auto" outperform intersection@1
at "auto": flag F1 on point, clustered, masking and irrelevant_columns, judged against
budgets v4?
